Lessons.Title: Different Compounding Intervals
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compare equal nominal annual rates applied at different compounding frequencies, identify the actual periodic interest rate and effective annual growth factor, and explain assumptions and limits of a mathematical comparison. Original first-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 17, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/17/preparation.html and student task https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/17/index.html (CC BY 4.0). No personal investment or borrowing advice is given.

Invented principal$1000 with nominal annual rate24%, no fees or tax. Annual compounding: A(y)=1000(1.24)^y for whole years. Monthly compounding: M(m)=1000(1+.24/12)^m=1000(1.02)^m; after12 months M(12)=1000(1.02)^12≈$1268.24. Annual A(1)=$1240, so additional compounding periods increase the modeled year-end amount by about$28.24 under these assumptions.

Effective annual rate of the monthly model is ((1.02)^12−1)×100≈26.8242%, not24%; nominal24% and periodic2% are different pieces of information. Comparing models fairly requires the same principal and elapsed time. For a quarterly model at6% per quarter, total after one year is1000(1.06)^4≈$1262.48.

Student task: write annual, quarterly and monthly functions, compare their one-year outputs and identify the correct time unit for each exponent. Explain what is held equal and which assumptions are omitted. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for period/rate conversion, correct powers and comparison, effective annual rate interpretation and reasoned caveats.

KeyConcepts.Title: Nominal and periodic rates
KeyConcepts.Definition: A nominal annual rate divided by number of compounding periods defines a periodic rate in this idealized convention.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For24% nominal and12 months, periodic rate2%.

KeyConcepts.Title: Effective annual factor
KeyConcepts.Definition: Apply the periodic multiplier for all compounding periods in a year.

KeyConcepts.Title: Comparable time units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Exponents represent numbers of periods, not necessarily years.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not use12 as a year count for monthly formula.
KeyConcepts.Example: At one year use A(1) versus M(12).
